subject: health
unitTitle: Safety, Injury Prevention, and Digital Life
title: Explicit model: emergency response and calling for help
focus: emergency response and calling for help
essentialQuestion: How do I prevent harm and respond well when something goes wrong?
materials: a basic first-aid kit for inspection with an adult
a properly fitted helmet or protective gear if relevant
keyPoints: Call 911 in the United States for fire, serious injury, someone not breathing, or a crime in progress.
Give what happened, the full address, and your name; stay on the line until told otherwise.
Check the scene is safe before approaching — do not become a second casualty.
Know your address and a guardian's number by heart; a locked phone can still call emergency services.
Prank calls take help away from someone who genuinely needs it.
privacySafeScenario: You find an adult collapsed and unresponsive at home and you are alone. Give the exact sequence, including what you say on the call.
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about emergency response and calling for help to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: State the most important rule or fact about emergency response and calling for help in your own words.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about emergency response and calling for help.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: First-aid content is taught as recognition and when-to-get-help, not as independent treatment. Any hands-on step may be observed, described, or demonstrated by the adult instead of performed by the learner.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about emergency response and calling for help under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, check that everyone in the household knows the home address and one emergency contact number by heart. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
